domain_label: Motion Honesty & Accessibility — The Permission Contract
purpose: The permission layer for the water-drop drill's motion: the binding contract that every animation graphux adds must be fully removable under prefers-reduced-motion without losing the timer, land on viz's quantized honest steps, imply no unmeasured mastery or adaptivity, stay at or above qcraft's ESL-readable fall floor, never become the selection target, write nothing to the learning model, and clear the seizure-flash limit — with every external accessibility/WCAG claim tagged for source-verification and every out-of-scope concern routed to its owning sibling.
assumptions: no observed dataset, accessibility audit, or user telemetry is supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the MDN and W3C/WAI accessibility sources are snippet-grade (direct WebFetch to the canonical publishers 403-blocked in this build env) and are tagged for re-verification before ship
the four sibling contracts (uxguide honesty, viz quantization, qcraft ESL floor, engage mechanic) are binding law that graphux obeys, not designs
exclusions: the aesthetic feel of the motion — curves, springs, squash-stretch, choreography (developed in kb1)
the render/performance envelope, frame budget, and library build-vs-adopt verdict (developed in kb3)
the numeric ESL floor value and item eligibility (owned by qcraft)
the step count, hue token, and static encoding (owned by viz); the mechanic and reward constants (owned by engage); the exact copy and onboarding (owned by uxguide)
the bkt_evidence/submitReview code path and the grade_source schema change (owned by learner+sched)

competency_questions.question: What four sibling contracts bound the motion graphux may add, and why is this the specialist's safety layer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: names uxguide honesty, reduced-motion removability, viz quantization, and qcraft's ESL floor as the binding permission envelope

competency_questions.question: How does prefers-reduced-motion and WCAG 2.3.3/C39 require the drill's motion to be removable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states the reduce signal, the essential/decorative split, and the 2.3.3/C39 disable-able-unless-essential rule, with sources tagged

competency_questions.question: What is the reduced-motion fallback for the drill, and what proves the drop physics is decorative?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: specifies a static countdown numeral/ring + step meter carrying 100% of the timer information as the removability proof

competency_questions.question: How do splash/particle bursts stay within the seizure-safety limit?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: caps bursts under the WCAG 2.3.1 three-flash threshold independent of the reduced-motion preference, with the number tagged

competency_questions.question: What honesty contract does graphux inherit, and why does it bind motion as well as copy?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: states the never-imply-precision/adaptivity/probability contract and applies it to animation, not just words

competency_questions.question: Why may no motion imply mastery, and what does the drill honestly reward?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: bans mastery/level-up-connoting motion and scopes the reward to session recognition-fluency only

competency_questions.question: Why is the moving drop never the selection target, and what does graphux animate instead?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: keeps selection on static buttons for construct validity and types every animation as feedback or timer, never a target

competency_questions.question: How does the water fill stay honestly quantized and colorblind-safe under animation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: lands motion on viz's floored steps with no between-step continuum and keeps the water in a cool token read by height+numeric

competency_questions.question: What is the ESL-readable fall floor, and how are timeouts framed as no-fault?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: holds the fall >= the per-card ESL floor and renders timeout as no-fault ('speed, not knowledge') with an untimed re-see

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: renders wrong/timeout feedback as informational and non-punitive and pre-explains the timeout framing in onboarding

competency_questions.question: How does graphux route concerns it does not own, and what is the final permission verdict?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: maps encoding to viz, mechanic to engage, honesty/onboarding to uxguide, item/floor to qcraft, and passes a motion only on a clean seven-point verdict

glossary.definition: A CSS media query signalling reduce | no-preference — a user preference to minimise non-essential motion, whose basis is that excessive motion can trigger vestibular disorders [FACT-source: MDN — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: direct-fetch 403-blocked]].

The split where motion is essential only if removing it changes information/functionality with no alternative; the drop physics is decorative and removable, the timer information is essential and retained [FACT-source: MDN — snippet-grade].
The success criterion requiring interaction-triggered motion to be disable-able unless essential, implemented via prefers-reduced-motion (technique C39) [FACT-source: W3C/WAI — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE]].
The seizure-safety criterion capping flashing content; splash/particle bursts must stay within its three-flashes threshold [FACT-source: W3C/WAI — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE]].
The static countdown numeral/ring + discrete step meter that replaces all drill animation under reduced-motion while conveying 100% of the timer/level information [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §1].
What the drill honestly rewards: correctness within a window = speed + accuracy, valid only where automaticity is the objective; never mastery or knowledge [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §1].
The construct-validity rule that answers are chosen on static option buttons (keys 1-4 / tap), never by catching the moving drop (which would test motor dexterity) [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §1].

The rule that the position/length fill is floored into discrete steps to read as a coarse counter, not a measured continuum, and that motion lands on those steps [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §1; viz dominance].
The invariant that the game only reads the learning model and never writes BKT/Elo/FSRS/day-box/CalibrationBin or persists the meter; timeout is not an FSRS 'Again' [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §3].

The evidence_class that isolates any logged timed data and excludes it by default from nightly BKT/Elo replay, diagnosis, and calibration bins — verified, not flag-and-trusted [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §3 invariant 3].

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for study_system_graphux_motion_honesty_accessibility_contract work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Frame the permission layer: the motion graphux may add to the drill is bounded by four sibling contracts — uxguide's honesty contract, the reduced-motion removability rule, viz's quantized-honest encoding, and qcraft's ESL fall-time floor [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §4]. This KB is what makes graphux SAFE: it defines what motion is permitted, not what motion feels good (kb1) or performs (kb3).

included: the four sibling constraints as the permission boundary
this KB as the safety spine of graphux

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a sibling specialist revises one of the four binding contracts

pros.claim: Naming the four contracts up front makes every motion checkable against a permission rule, not taste
pros.example: asking whether a proposed splash clears reduced-motion, honesty, quantization, and ESL before it ships

cons.claim: The permission frame can read as pure restriction and dampen the feel graphux is meant to add
cons.example: treating the contract as a veto list rather than a design envelope

failure_modes: treating the contracts as optional guidelines
authoring feel without checking it against the permission layer
acceptance_tests: the frame names all four sibling contracts and positions this KB as the binding permission layer
revisit_triggers: a sibling revises one of the four contracts

nodes.definition: The prefers-reduced-motion media query signals reduce | no-preference, expressing a user preference to minimise non-essential motion; excessive motion is a vestibular-disorder trigger [FACT-source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-reduced-motion — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: direct-fetch 403-blocked]]. graphux must honor this signal for every decorative motion in the drill.

included: the reduce|no-preference signal and its vestibular basis
honoring the signal for decorative motion

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a direct fetch confirms or revises the prefers-reduced-motion semantics

pros.claim: Honoring the OS signal respects a real accessibility need at the platform level
pros.example: disabling the drop physics automatically when the learner's OS requests reduced motion

cons.claim: The MDN definition here is snippet-grade (direct fetch 403-blocked) and must be re-confirmed before ship
cons.example: quoting the exact media-query semantics as FACT without the source-verify tag

failure_modes: ignoring the OS reduced-motion preference
treating reduced-motion as an edge case rather than a default path
acceptance_tests: the reduce|no-preference signal and its vestibular rationale are stated with the source tagged for verification
revisit_triggers: a direct source check revises the media-query semantics

nodes.definition: Motion is ESSENTIAL only if removing it fundamentally changes the information or functionality with no alternative (loading indicators, validation feedback, game mechanics); hover/parallax/entrance animation is DECORATIVE [FACT-source: MDN prefers-reduced-motion — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: direct-fetch 403-blocked]]. In the drill: the drop PHYSICS is decorative and fully removable; the TIMER INFORMATION is essential and never removed.

included: the essential/decorative definition
the drop-physics=decorative, timer=essential mapping

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a direct fetch revises the essential-vs-decorative definition

pros.claim: Classifying drop physics as decorative and the timer as essential makes the removability rule precise
pros.example: removing the fall animation under reduced-motion while keeping the countdown that carries the timer

cons.claim: The essential/decorative line can be argued; mislabeling essential motion as decorative would strip information
cons.example: calling the countdown itself decorative and losing the timer under reduced-motion

failure_modes: classifying the timer information as decorative and removing it
classifying pure polish as essential and forcing it on
acceptance_tests: drop physics is classified decorative/removable and the timer information essential/retained, per the MDN split
revisit_triggers: a direct source check revises the essential/decorative definition

nodes.definition: WCAG 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions requires that motion triggered by interaction be disable-able unless the animation is essential [FACT-source: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/animation-from-interactions.html — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: direct-fetch 403-blocked]]; technique C39 implements it via prefers-reduced-motion [FACT-source: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/css/C39 — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE]]. The drill's interaction-triggered rise/splash are covered by this criterion.

included: the 2.3.3 disable-able-unless-essential rule
C39 as the prefers-reduced-motion implementation
excluded: the pixel implementation of the toggle

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a direct fetch confirms or revises WCAG 2.3.3 / C39

pros.claim: Anchoring removability to a named WCAG criterion makes the rule auditable, not aspirational
pros.example: citing 2.3.3/C39 as the standard the rise/splash removal must satisfy

cons.claim: The WCAG wording here is snippet-grade and must be re-confirmed by direct fetch before it is asserted as law
cons.example: quoting the exact 2.3.3 normative text as FACT without the source-verify tag

failure_modes: treating removability as optional polish rather than a WCAG obligation
conflating 2.3.3 (interaction motion) with 2.3.1 (flashing)
acceptance_tests: interaction-triggered motion is specified disable-able per 2.3.3/C39 with the sources tagged for verification
revisit_triggers: a direct source check revises the 2.3.3/C39 wording

nodes.definition: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (and any in-app toggle) every drill animation is removed/replaced by a STATIC countdown numeral/ring + a discrete step meter that conveys 100% of the drill's information [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §1]. The fallback is the proof that the drop physics is decorative: nothing informational is lost when it is gone.

included: the static numeral/ring + step-meter fallback
100%-information-parity as the removability proof

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a reduced-motion audit finds the fallback loses information

pros.claim: A concrete static fallback makes reduced-motion a first-class path, not an afterthought that drops information
pros.example: showing a numeric countdown and a stepped meter with the fall physics fully disabled

cons.claim: If the fallback cannot carry the full timer information, the whole motion design is invalid and must be redesigned
cons.example: a fallback that omits the remaining time and leaves the learner blind to the window

failure_modes: a fallback that loses the timer information
treating the fallback as lower-fidelity rather than information-complete
acceptance_tests: the reduced-motion fallback conveys 100% of the timer and level information via a static numeral/ring + step meter
revisit_triggers: the fallback is found to lose any information and must be redesigned

nodes.definition: WCAG 2.3.1 constrains flashing to protect photosensitive users (the three-flashes threshold); splash/particle bursts must respect this hard flash cap [FACT-source: WCAG 2.3-family — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: direct-fetch 403-blocked]]. This is a safety floor independent of the reduced-motion preference — it binds even when motion is allowed.

included: the three-flash seizure cap on bursts
a safety floor independent of reduced-motion

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a direct fetch confirms or revises WCAG 2.3.1

pros.claim: A hard flash cap protects photosensitive users regardless of their motion preference
pros.example: limiting the splash burst to below the three-flash threshold even for users who allow motion

cons.claim: The exact 2.3.1 threshold is snippet-grade here and must be verified before it is treated as a precise number
cons.example: citing a specific flashes-per-second figure as FACT without the source-verify tag

failure_modes: a bright rapid burst that approaches the seizure threshold
treating flash safety as covered by reduced-motion alone
acceptance_tests: splash/particle bursts are specified within the three-flash seizure limit, with the WCAG number tagged for verification
revisit_triggers: a direct source check revises the 2.3.1 threshold

nodes.definition: graphux inherits uxguide's honest-translation contract: a surface must never upgrade a heuristic constant into a probability, imply a precision the value lacks, or imply an adaptivity the app does not have [FACT — uxguide.role/glossary]. For graphux this binds MOTION and copy together: an animation that implies the app is adapting or measuring is as dishonest as words that do.

included: the inherited never-imply-precision/adaptivity/probability rule
motion as subject to the same honesty as copy
excluded: the specific reward copy (uxguide authors it)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: uxguide revises the honest-translation contract

pros.claim: Extending the honesty contract to motion stops animation from smuggling in claims words are forbidden to make
pros.example: refusing an animation that pulses as if the app is 'thinking'/adapting when it is not

cons.claim: Motion is a subtler honesty channel than copy and its implications are easier to overlook
cons.example: missing that a smooth ramp implies a measured continuum the counter does not have

failure_modes: treating motion as exempt from the honesty contract
implying adaptivity/measurement through animation
acceptance_tests: the honest-translation contract is applied to motion as well as copy, forbidding implied precision/adaptivity/probability
revisit_triggers: uxguide revises the honest-translation contract

nodes.definition: No motion, burst, or 'level-up' flourish may connote durable progress, mastery, or adaptivity; the drill rewards recognition fluency only and is flagged as such [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §1]. A celebratory animation that reads as 'you have mastered this' is a lie the water meter must never tell.

included: the ban on mastery/level-up-connoting motion
recognition-fluency-only as the honest reward

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a review finds a motion flourish implying mastery

pros.claim: Banning mastery-connoting flourishes keeps the drill's reward honestly scoped to session fluency
pros.example: using a modest session-scoped confirmation instead of a triumphant mastery fanfare

cons.claim: The line between a satisfying confirmation and a mastery-implying flourish is a judgement call
cons.example: a burst intended as fun that a learner reads as durable achievement

failure_modes: a level-up burst that reads as durable mastery
framing fluency gains as knowledge gains via motion
acceptance_tests: no motion or burst reads as durable mastery/adaptivity; the reward is flagged session recognition-fluency
revisit_triggers: a review finds a flourish reading as mastery

nodes.definition: What the drill honestly rewards is correctness-within-a-window = speed + accuracy = recognition fluency, valid ONLY where automaticity is the actual objective [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §1]. The water meter is a fluency signal, never a mastery or knowledge signal, and its motion must carry that scoped meaning.

included: correctness-in-window = recognition fluency
validity limited to automaticity objectives

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: qcraft revises where recognition-fluency reward is valid

pros.claim: Scoping the reward to recognition fluency keeps the meter honest about what speed+accuracy actually measures
pros.example: labelling the meter a session fluency signal, not progress toward exam mastery

cons.claim: Recognition fluency is easily conflated with mastery by users, so the scoping must be reinforced everywhere
cons.example: a learner assuming a full water meter means they know the material deeply

failure_modes: selling fluency as mastery
applying the drill where automaticity is not the objective
acceptance_tests: the reward is scoped to recognition fluency and never presented via motion as mastery or knowledge
revisit_triggers: qcraft narrows or widens the automaticity-valid item set

nodes.definition: Selection targets are the STATIC option buttons (keys 1-4 / tap) — NEVER a moving drop; clicking a moving target is a motor-dexterity test and is construct-invalid [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §1]. graphux animates FEEDBACK, never the hit-target. This is an absolute construct-validity boundary.

included: static option buttons as the only selection targets
the moving drop is never clickable

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a build introduces a clickable moving target

pros.claim: Keeping selection on static buttons preserves construct validity — the drill tests recognition, not dexterity
pros.example: binding the answer to key presses on fixed buttons while the drop animates purely as a timer

cons.claim: A moving drop is tempting as an interactive target and a build could accidentally make it clickable
cons.example: a tap on the falling drop accidentally registering as an answer

failure_modes: making the moving drop a selection target
turning the drill into a reaction/dexterity test
acceptance_tests: selection is confirmed on static buttons (keys 1-4/tap) and no path lets a tap on the moving drop answer
revisit_triggers: a build path is found that makes the drop clickable

nodes.definition: graphux animates the FEEDBACK (the rise, splash, decay) and the TIMER (the fall), never the selection target. The fall communicates remaining time; it is not a thing to catch. This node operationalises STATIC_TARGET_SELECTION for every animated element: each is feedback or timer, none is interactive.

included: classifying each animation as feedback or timer, never target
the fall as a timer, not a catchable object

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a usability check finds a feedback element reads as interactive

pros.claim: Explicitly typing each animation as feedback/timer prevents any element drifting into an interactive target
pros.example: documenting the fall as a non-interactive timer so no gesture handler is attached to it

cons.claim: Feedback animations near the buttons could still be mistaken for interactive affordances
cons.example: a splash overlapping a button that a learner tries to tap

failure_modes: attaching interaction handlers to feedback/timer animations
letting a feedback element look like a button
acceptance_tests: every animated element is typed feedback or timer and none carries a selection handler or reads as a target
revisit_triggers: a feedback element is found to read as interactive

nodes.definition: Fill = position/length is the MOST accurate perceptual channel, so it must be quantized into discrete steps (like DayBox floor(...*20)) to signal 'coarse counter', not 'measured continuum' [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §1; viz conflicts_and_dominance: 'honest quantization dominates a smooth precise ramp']. graphux's rise/decay must land on these steps and animate only between them.

included: fill quantized into discrete honest steps
motion lands on and moves between steps only
excluded: the number of steps (viz owns it)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: viz revises the quantization step count

pros.claim: Landing motion on viz's discrete steps keeps the meter reading as a coarse counter, matching the data's real resolution
pros.example: snapping the settled water level to the floored step even if the animation eased past it

cons.claim: A fluid animation naturally wants to show intermediate values, tempting a false continuum
cons.example: an eased rise briefly displaying a value between two honest steps

failure_modes: rendering a smooth continuum that fakes measured precision
overshooting past the honest step and misreading progress
acceptance_tests: the rise/decay land exactly on viz's floored steps and never display a settled between-step continuum
revisit_triggers: viz changes the quantization step count

nodes.definition: The water hue is a cool/cyan token OUTSIDE the mastery green/yellow/red palette, and level reads by HEIGHT + NUMERIC LABEL, never green/red water alone (colorblind-safe) [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §1]. graphux does not choose the hue (viz does) but must not add color-carried motion meaning that reintroduces the mastery palette or a color-only distinction.

included: cool/cyan token outside the mastery palette
height+numeric redundancy, never color-only

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: viz revises the water hue token or palette separation

pros.claim: Keeping the water hue outside the mastery palette prevents motion from borrowing mastery's color meaning
pros.example: never flashing the water green on a hit, which would collide with the mastery-known color

cons.claim: Motion effects can sneak color in (a colored glow/flash) and reintroduce a color-only distinction
cons.example: a green celebratory glow that a colorblind user cannot distinguish and that borrows mastery green

failure_modes: adding a motion color that re-enters the mastery palette
carrying a distinction on flash color alone
acceptance_tests: no motion introduces a color that re-enters the mastery palette or carries a distinction on color alone
revisit_triggers: viz revises the hue token or palette separation

nodes.definition: The fall window must exceed a floor that lets a domain-lite ESL learner read the stem + all options once — else the drill silently tests English reading rate. Fall time is a per-card ESTIMATE calibrated to option count + ESL reading rate, with a readable floor; cinematic pacing may LENGTHEN but never UNDERCUT it [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §1; qcraft owns item validity/ESL fairness].

included: the ESL-readable floor on the fall window
feel may lengthen, never undercut the floor
excluded: the floor's numeric value (qcraft calibrates it)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: qcraft recalibrates the ESL-readable fall floor

pros.claim: A readable floor keeps the drill a recognition test rather than a hidden English reading-speed test
pros.example: holding the fall at or above the option-count-calibrated floor even when a snappier fall is wanted

cons.claim: The floor is a per-card estimate not yet empirically calibrated, so it must be treated as provisional
cons.example: treating an un-calibrated fall time as a validated timer

failure_modes: shortening the fall below the readable floor for feel
treating fall time as a fixed cinematic constant
acceptance_tests: the animated fall duration is >= the per-card ESL floor in every path, checked against qcraft's estimate
revisit_triggers: qcraft recalibrates the ESL-readable floor

nodes.definition: A missed drop has no chosen_option_id → no misconception, no knowledge verdict, and it is NOT an FSRS 'Again' [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §1]. The UI reads 'Correct — but the drop fell first. Speed, not knowledge,' with an offer to re-see the item untimed. graphux's timeout animation must carry this no-fault meaning and write no learning evidence.

included: timeout != wrong, != FSRS Again
no-fault timeout motion + untimed re-see offer

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: sched/learner revises how timeout is scored

pros.claim: Rendering timeout as no-fault prevents the drill from punishing slow reading as if it were not knowing
pros.example: a gentle non-punitive timeout animation plus an untimed re-see, never a red X

cons.claim: A timeout animation can easily read as failure/shame if styled like a wrong answer
cons.example: a harsh buzzer/shake on timeout that implies the learner got it wrong

failure_modes: styling timeout as a wrong-answer failure
letting a timeout write an FSRS Again or any knowledge verdict
acceptance_tests: the timeout animation is no-fault, offers an untimed re-see, and writes no learning verdict
revisit_triggers: sched/learner revises timeout scoring

nodes.definition: The drill has no shame loop on a wrong answer or a timeout, and first-run onboarding pre-explains the timeout framing [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §1]. graphux's error/timeout feedback must be informational, never punitive — a study tool that shames a slow ESL reader is both cruel and construct-invalid.

included: no punitive/shame feedback on wrong or timeout
onboarding pre-explains the timeout framing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: uxguide revises the no-shame or onboarding framing

pros.claim: Non-punitive feedback keeps the learner engaged and stops the drill from testing composure instead of recall
pros.example: a neutral corrective animation instead of a shaming failure sequence

cons.claim: Removing all negative feedback can blur the correct/incorrect distinction the learner needs
cons.example: softening a wrong-answer signal so much the learner misses that they erred

failure_modes: a punitive shame animation on error/timeout
blurring the corrective signal entirely
acceptance_tests: wrong/timeout feedback is informational and non-punitive, and the timeout framing is pre-explained in onboarding
revisit_triggers: uxguide revises the no-shame/onboarding framing

nodes.definition: The arrow is one-way: no motion event or timed outcome writes BKT P(L) / Elo θ / item b, FSRS CardState.due / revlog, WaterMeter persistence, day-box pct, or CalibrationBin; timeout != FSRS 'Again' [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §3 invariants 1,2,3,8,9]. graphux only ever READS the learning model to drive display; it never writes it. This is a hard-stop, re-verified-never-reverted boundary.

included: the one-way read-only arrow
no motion/timed outcome writes any model/scheduler state

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change touches the bkt_evidence/submitReview/persistence path

pros.claim: A hard read-only rule guarantees the game can never corrupt the learning signal it visualises
pros.example: the rise animation reading the correctness result but writing nothing back to BKT/FSRS

cons.claim: The bkt_evidence path was silently broken once, so flag-and-trust is insufficient and every touch needs re-verification
cons.example: assuming a write is harmless because it is 'just' the meter, then persisting it

failure_modes: writing any learning-model or scheduler state from a motion/timed event
persisting the WaterMeter
acceptance_tests: an audit shows no motion or timed outcome writes BKT/Elo/FSRS/day-box/CalibrationBin/WaterMeter state
revisit_triggers: any change touches the bkt_evidence/submitReview path

nodes.definition: If any timed data is logged at all, it is quarantined as a distinct evidence_class = 'game_timed' (extend grade_source), excluded by default from every nightly BKT/Elo replay, diagnosis, and calibration bin [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §3 invariant 3]. Flag-and-trust is insufficient; the quarantine must be verified, and no graphux motion may depend on the timed data feeding the model.

included: evidence_class='game_timed' quarantine
exclusion from replay/diagnosis/calibration by default

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the grade_source/evidence_class schema or replay filter changes

pros.claim: Quarantining timed data as a distinct class stops it silently contaminating the learning replay
pros.example: tagging any logged drill outcome game_timed and excluding it from the nightly BKT replay

cons.claim: A quarantine is only safe if verified; a mislabeled or leaked class re-poisons the model
cons.example: a game_timed row slipping into the calibration bin because the filter was assumed, not tested

failure_modes: relying on a flag without verifying the exclusion
letting timed data feed the model by default
acceptance_tests: timed data, if logged, is tagged game_timed and its exclusion from replay/diagnosis/calibration is verified
revisit_triggers: the grade_source/evidence_class schema changes

nodes.definition: The WaterMeter is ephemeral session state that resets each session and writes nowhere; its decay is session-only (a multi-day decay would create a pull to review early = a spacing violation) [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §1 non-persistence invariant]. graphux's meter/decay animation must reflect a value that never survives the session.

included: WaterMeter resets each session, persists nothing
session-only decay to protect spacing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the water_decay_timescale open decision is resolved

pros.claim: Session-only, non-persistent meter state guarantees the game cannot create a cross-day pull that breaks spacing
pros.example: the meter resetting to empty at session start with no stored history

cons.claim: Users may expect their 'progress' to persist, and a reset can feel like lost work if not framed
cons.example: a learner frustrated that yesterday's full meter is gone, mistaking it for real progress

failure_modes: persisting the meter across sessions
a multi-day decay that pulls the learner to review early
acceptance_tests: the meter animation reflects session-only, non-persistent state and no multi-day decay is rendered
revisit_triggers: the water_decay_timescale decision is set

nodes.definition: The four seams graphux must not cross: viz (STATIC visual encoding / Bertin variables — graphux owns motion, not static meaning), engage (the mechanic + reward psychology — graphux owns how it feels frame-to-frame), uxguide (the honesty/onboarding contract graphux must obey), qcraft (the timed-item construct + fall-time floor). graphux receives the honest quantized level and static targets as INPUTS and only animates them.

included: the four sibling seams and who owns what
graphux animates inputs it is handed, never authors them
excluded: the internals of each sibling's domain

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a sibling ownership boundary is revised

pros.example: routing a 'change the step count' request to viz rather than re-quantizing in graphux

cons.claim: Seams can blur in practice when a feel change seems to require a mechanic/encoding change
cons.example: wanting to alter rise-per-hit to 'make it feel better', which is engage's mechanic

failure_modes: absorbing a sibling's decision into graphux
animating a datum before the owning sibling has fixed it

nodes.definition: Synthesis: emit the permission verdict for a proposed drill motion — pass only if it is fully removable under reduced-motion with the timer preserved, lands on viz's quantized honest steps, implies no unmeasured mastery/adaptivity, stays >= the ESL floor, is never the selection target, writes nothing to the model, and clears the flash cap. Any failure routes to the owning sibling. Every external accessibility/WCAG claim carries its source-verify tag.

included: the seven-point permission verdict
route-to-owner on any failure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a sibling contract or an external accessibility source is revised

pros.claim: A single seven-point permission gate makes any motion's safety decidable and its failures routable
pros.example: running a proposed splash through removability/quantization/honesty/ESL/target/no-write/flash before approval

cons.claim: The verdict is only as sound as its inputs; a snippet-grade WCAG claim asserted as law weakens it
cons.example: approving a motion on an unverified accessibility number without the source-verify tag

failure_modes: approving a motion that fails any of the seven checks
asserting an unverified accessibility number as law in the verdict
acceptance_tests: the permission verdict applies all seven checks, routes failures to owners, and tags every external claim for verification
revisit_triggers: a sibling contract or WCAG source is revised

conflict_axes.name: cinematic_pacing_vs_esl_readable_floor
conflict_axes.description: Slower, more dramatic falls feel better, but the fall duration is floored by the ESL-readable window.
poles: never shorten below the ESL floor
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the ESL floor dominates: feel may lengthen the fall but never undercut the readable window

conflict_axes.name: juice_appeal_vs_no_mastery_implication
conflict_axes.description: A triumphant celebration is appealing but can read as durable mastery the app has not measured.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the honesty contract dominates: no motion may imply mastery, adaptivity, or measured progress

conflict_axes.name: smooth_fill_vs_quantized_honesty
conflict_axes.description: A continuous fill is more fluid but implies a measured continuum the counter lacks.
poles: animate only between discrete honest steps
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: quantized honesty dominates: motion lands on viz's floored steps and shows no between-step continuum

conflict_axes.name: interactive_moving_drop_vs_construct_validity
conflict_axes.description: A catchable moving drop is engaging but turns the drill into a motor-dexterity test.
poles: make the drop a clickable target
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: construct validity dominates: the moving drop is never a target; selection stays on static buttons

conflict_axes.name: expressive_timeout_vs_no_shame
conflict_axes.description: An expressive failure animation is satisfying feedback but shames a slow ESL reader.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: no-shame dominates: timeout is no-fault, offers an untimed re-see, and is never styled as failure

conflict_axes.name: persistent_progress_vs_ephemeral_meter
conflict_axes.description: Persisting the meter feels like real progress but creates a cross-day pull that breaks spacing.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: ephemerality dominates: the meter is session-only and persists nothing, protecting the spacing schedule

conflict_axes.name: useful_timed_signal_vs_model_integrity
conflict_axes.description: Timed data looks like a useful fluency signal but feeding it to the model corrupts BKT/Elo/FSRS.
poles: let timed data inform the model
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: model integrity dominates: timed data is quarantined and excluded from replay by default, verified not trusted

conflict_axes.name: richer_motion_vs_reduced_motion_removability
conflict_axes.description: Richer, more layered motion is more alive but harder to fully remove without losing information.
poles: keep every decorative motion cleanly removable
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: removability dominates: every decorative motion must fully remove to a static, information-complete fallback

conflict_axes.name: bright_splash_vs_seizure_safety
conflict_axes.description: A bright rapid splash burst is exciting but can approach the three-flash seizure threshold.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: seizure safety dominates: bursts stay within the three-flash limit regardless of appeal

conflict_axes.name: in_house_reinterpretation_vs_sibling_ownership
conflict_axes.description: Reinterpreting a step count or floor inside graphux is faster than routing to the owner.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: sibling ownership dominates: graphux animates inputs and routes any encoding/mechanic/floor change to its owner

edge_cases.description: A learner enables prefers-reduced-motion mid-session while a fall is animating.
edge_cases.mitigation: swap immediately to the static numeral/ring + step meter without losing the current remaining-time information

edge_cases.description: The reduced-motion fallback omits the remaining time, leaving the learner unable to judge the window.
edge_cases.mitigation: redesign the fallback to carry 100% of the timer information; the motion design is invalid until it does

edge_cases.description: A celebratory splash on a hit reads to the learner as 'mastered'.
edge_cases.mitigation: reduce the celebration to a session-scoped confirmation and reinforce the fluency-only framing

edge_cases.description: A build attaches a tap handler to the falling drop so catching it answers.
edge_cases.mitigation: remove the handler; selection must remain on the static option buttons only

edge_cases.description: The eased rise briefly shows the water between two quantized steps.
edge_cases.mitigation: snap the settled level to the floored step and damp any overshoot so no between-step value persists

edge_cases.description: A timeout is styled with a red X and buzzer like a wrong answer.
edge_cases.mitigation: restyle as no-fault ('the drop fell first — speed, not knowledge') with an untimed re-see offer

edge_cases.description: A developer persists the WaterMeter to restore it next session.
edge_cases.mitigation: remove persistence; the meter resets each session and a multi-day decay is forbidden (spacing violation)

edge_cases.description: A timed drill outcome is written into the nightly BKT replay.
edge_cases.mitigation: hard-stop; tag game_timed and verify exclusion from replay/diagnosis/calibration before any writer ships

edge_cases.description: A motion glow flashes the water green on a correct hit.
edge_cases.mitigation: remove the color; keep the water in its cool token and carry the hit via height/numeric, not color

edge_cases.description: A feel request asks to raise rise-per-hit to make progress feel faster.
edge_cases.trigger: feel change needs a mechanic change
edge_cases.mitigation: route to engage; graphux animates the mechanic it is handed and does not change rise-per-hit

edge_cases.description: A splash burst flashes several times per second on a combo of quick hits.
edge_cases.mitigation: throttle and dim the burst so repeated hits cannot exceed the three-flash seizure limit

edge_cases.description: The ESL floor is not yet calibrated and a fall time is shipped as final.
edge_cases.trigger: uncalibrated fall time treated as final
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the fall time as a provisional per-card ESTIMATE and route to qcraft for empirical calibration before ship

workflow.action: Frame the four sibling permission contracts
workflow.description: Name uxguide honesty, reduced-motion removability, viz quantization, and qcraft's ESL floor as the binding envelope for any motion.
workflow.gate: all four contracts are named before a motion is evaluated

workflow.action: Classify the motion essential vs decorative
workflow.description: Decide whether the motion carries information (essential) or is polish (decorative); drop physics is decorative, the timer essential.
workflow.gate: every drill motion is classified and the timer is held essential

workflow.description: Define the static numeral/ring + step-meter fallback and verify it conveys 100% of the timer/level information.
workflow.gate: the fallback loses no information under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce

workflow.action: Check honesty: no mastery, quantized, cool hue
workflow.description: Confirm the motion lands on viz's discrete steps, implies no mastery/adaptivity, and adds no color that re-enters the mastery palette.
workflow.gate: no motion implies mastery or shows a between-step continuum or a color-only distinction

workflow.description: Verify the animated fall duration is >= the per-card ESL floor in every path against qcraft's estimate.
workflow.gate: the fall never undercuts the readable window

workflow.description: Confirm selection is only on static buttons and no animated element is a hit-target.
workflow.gate: the moving drop and all feedback carry no selection handler

workflow.action: Check the one-way arrow and quarantine
workflow.description: Audit that no motion/timed outcome writes the model/scheduler/meter and that any logged timed data is quarantined game_timed.
workflow.gate: nothing writes BKT/Elo/FSRS/day-box/CalibrationBin/meter; timed data is quarantined

workflow.description: Verify splash/particle bursts stay within the three-flash seizure limit.

workflow.action: Route out-of-scope asks via the seam map
workflow.description: Send encoding to viz, mechanic to engage, honesty/onboarding to uxguide, item/floor to qcraft.
workflow.gate: every out-of-scope concern reaches its owning sibling

workflow.description: Pass the motion only if it clears all seven checks; otherwise route the failure; tag every external accessibility claim for verification.
workflow.gate: the motion is approved only on a clean seven-point pass with sources tagged

priority_rationale: The permission frame and its accessibility/honesty/construct/no-write pillars come first because they gate every motion; the fallback, quantization, ESL-floor, target-integrity, and one-way-arrow rules operationalise them; the seam map and the seven-point verdict close the layer so any motion is decidably safe or routed to its owner.

dominance_rules.rationale: a decorative motion that cannot fully remove without losing information is disallowed
dominance_rules.trigger: a motion cannot degrade to an information-complete static fallback
dominance_rules.action: simplify until the fallback carries 100% of the information

dominance_rules.rule: The essential timer dominates the decorative physics
dominance_rules.rationale: the drop physics is decorative but the timer it visualises is essential
dominance_rules.action: retain the timer as a static numeral/ring + step meter

dominance_rules.rule: The ESL-readable floor dominates cinematic pacing
dominance_rules.rationale: a fall below the floor silently tests English reading rate
dominance_rules.trigger: a pacing change nears/undercuts the ESL floor
dominance_rules.action: hold the floor; lengthen only, never shorten

dominance_rules.rule: Quantized honesty dominates a smooth fill
dominance_rules.rationale: a continuous fill fakes a measured continuum
dominance_rules.trigger: a motion shows a between-step value
dominance_rules.action: land on viz's floored steps and damp overshoot

dominance_rules.rule: The no-mastery contract dominates celebratory juice
dominance_rules.rationale: a mastery-style flourish claims durable progress the app has not measured

dominance_rules.rule: Construct validity dominates an interactive drop
dominance_rules.rationale: catching a moving target tests dexterity, not recognition
dominance_rules.trigger: the moving drop is proposed as a target
dominance_rules.action: keep selection on static buttons; the drop is a timer only

dominance_rules.rationale: shaming a slow ESL reader tests composure, not recall
dominance_rules.action: render no-fault feedback with an untimed re-see

dominance_rules.rule: Model integrity dominates a useful timed signal
dominance_rules.rationale: a game write can corrupt BKT/Elo/FSRS irreversibly
dominance_rules.trigger: a timed outcome would touch the model/scheduler
dominance_rules.action: hard-stop; read-only, quarantine, re-verify never revert

dominance_rules.rule: Ephemerality dominates a persistent progress feel
dominance_rules.rationale: a persisted/multi-day meter pulls early review and breaks spacing
dominance_rules.trigger: the meter would persist or decay across days

dominance_rules.rationale: re-deciding a sibling's datum in graphux breaks the seam
dominance_rules.trigger: a fix seems to need a step/mechanic/floor change
dominance_rules.action: route to the owning sibling and animate the returned input

dominance_rules.rationale: a flash over the threshold can trigger a seizure
dominance_rules.trigger: a burst approaches the three-flash limit
dominance_rules.action: throttle and dim until it clears WCAG 2.3.1

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the reduced-motion fallback carries all information before building the animation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rebuilding the whole motion after the fallback is found to drop the timer

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the motion lands on viz's quantized steps from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-authoring a smooth fill that faked measured precision

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check the fall against the ESL floor before finalising pacing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-timing the fall after it is found to breach the readable window

anti_rework_rules.rule: Type every animated element feedback-or-timer up front
anti_rework_rules.prevents: removing an accidental selection handler discovered late on the moving drop

anti_rework_rules.rule: Audit the one-way arrow before any logging path ships
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reverting a model write that corrupted BKT/Elo/FSRS after the fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Quarantine timed data as game_timed and verify exclusion, never flag-and-trust
anti_rework_rules.prevents: cleaning contaminated calibration bins after a leaked class

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the meter ephemeral and session-only from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unwinding a persistence/multi-day-decay feature that broke spacing

anti_rework_rules.rule: Route encoding/mechanic/floor asks to the owner immediately
anti_rework_rules.prevents: undoing an in-house re-quantization that diverged from viz

iteration_protocol.trigger: a direct fetch confirms or revises the MDN prefers-reduced-motion definition, WCAG 2.3.3/C39, and WCAG 2.3.1 (all snippet-grade / 403-blocked here)
iteration_protocol.action: replace UNVERIFIED-SOURCE tags with cited FACTs and re-check any removability/flash rule that leaned on a revised wording

iteration_protocol.trigger: qcraft recalibrates the ESL-readable fall floor empirically
iteration_protocol.action: re-check the fall-floor rule and the timeout framing against the new floor

iteration_protocol.trigger: the grade_source/evidence_class schema or nightly replay filter changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the game_timed quarantine and the one-way arrow end to end

iteration_protocol.trigger: viz revises the step count, hue token, or palette separation
iteration_protocol.action: re-check the quantized-encoding and cool-hue rules against the new encoding

iteration_protocol.trigger: uxguide revises the honesty or onboarding/no-shame framing
iteration_protocol.action: re-check the mastery-flourish ban and the no-shame rule

iteration_protocol.trigger: the water_decay_timescale open decision is resolved
iteration_protocol.action: re-check the ephemeral-meter rule against the chosen timescale

iteration_protocol.trigger: a sibling ownership boundary is revised
iteration_protocol.action: update the seam map and re-route affected escalations
